articles.content_id:
Ngopi Sudah Jadi Kebiasaan, Kedai Tumbuh Tiga Kali Lipat — dan yang Tumbuh Paling Cepat Sekarang Ada di Trotoar

Konsumsi kopi nasional 288 ribu ton dan 46% orang ngopi tiap hari. Kedai tumbuh hampir 3x lipat, tapi kanal yang tumbuh paling cepat saat ini justru gerobak di trotoar — lewat satu hal sederhana.
Oleh: Redaksi Kabar Kopi | Ganjar Satyanagara · Oktober 2026

Pertanyaan yang jarang diajukan di industri kopi Indonesia bukan “apakah pasar tumbuh” — semua orang tahu ia tumbuh. Pertanyaan yang tepat: di segmen mana pertumbuhan itu terjadi, seberapa cepat, dan apa artinya bagi masing-masing pelaku?

Saya mulai dari angka yang paling sering dikutip dan paling jarang dicerna. Kementerian Perindustrian mencatat konsumsi kopi nasional 2025 mencapai 288 ribu ton, setara 1,03 kg per kapita, dengan proyeksi pertumbuhan pasar 3,61 persen per tahun hingga 2029. Angka itu terdengar administratif. Tapi ada satu hal menarik di baliknya: 288 ribu ton itu penyerapan domestik murni — dan mengingat laporan kami sebelumnya, permintaan domestik inilah salah satu faktor yang menahan harga di hulu tetap tinggi saat harga global turun. Pasar dalam negeri sudah bukan pelengkap ekspor. Ia fondasi.

Sekarang ke perilaku konsumen, karena pasar bukan angka — pasar adalah kebiasaan.

Survei Jakpat 2025 terhadap 1.002 responden menemukan bahwa 46 persen konsumen minum kopi setiap hari. Bukan setiap minggu. Setiap hari. Waktu favoritnya bukan pagi hari seperti stereotip Barat, melainkan sore (35 persen) dan setelah sarapan (34 persen). Dan tujuan utamanya berkumpul serta mengobrol (44 persen), bukan sekadar mencari kafein untuk fokus (34 persen).

Ini detail kecil yang penting. Kopi sudah menjadi infrastruktur sosial — tempat bertemu, alasan berkumpul, pengisi jeda. Tapi perlu hati-hati di sini: kebiasaan ngopi sore di kedai dengan teman, dan kebiasaan menyeduh kopi instan di rumah sebelum berangkat kerja, adalah dua kebiasaan yang berbeda — beda tempat, beda fungsi, dan tidak saling menggantikan. Survei Jakpat memang mencatatnya dalam satu tabel preferensi produk: kopi susu instan dikonsumsi rutin oleh 53 persen responden, kopi hitam instan 43 persen, es kopi susu dari kafe 28 persen. Angka-angka ini sering dibaca seolah ada “tangga” — dari instan naik ke kafe. Saya justru tidak membaca begitu. Tiga angka itu menggambarkan tiga kesempatan minum yang berbeda, bukan tiga tingkat kedewasaan konsumen. Ada pasar rumah, ada pasar kedai, dan keduanya besar dengan caranya sendiri.

Dan pasar kedai sendiri sedang berubah bentuk.

Kemenperin mencatat jumlah kedai kopi tumbuh hampir tiga kali lipat dalam tiga tahun terakhir — ditopang struktur demografi yang ekstrem, di mana lebih dari 53 persen penduduk Indonesia adalah Gen Z dan milenial. Tapi di dalam kanal racikan barista itu sendiri, muncul sub-kanal yang tumbuh paling cepat saat ini: kopi keliling modern.

Survei Cimigo Oktober 2025 — 247 responden, sampel kecil tetapi tajam — menunjukkan 49 persen konsumen kopi racikan barista, dan di antara mereka pembelian rata-rata 4,5 kali per minggu. Untuk kanal khusus kopi racikan: coffee shop masih utama (88 persen), minimarket 48 persen, dan kopi keliling modern 47 persen.

Satu catatan kehati-hatian sebelum angka itu dibaca lebih jauh: kopi keliling bukan pengganti coffee shop. Orang yang ngopi sambil meeting dua jam di kedai tidak pindah ke trotoar; sebaliknya, konsumen yang butuh kopi racikan cepat di perjalanan sering tidak sempat masuk kedai. Kopi keliling melayani kesempatan minum yang selama ini tidak terlayani — bukan mencuri pelanggan dari kedai. Keduanya tumbuh di kesempatan yang berbeda.

Lalu mengapa kopi keliling bisa tumbuh secepat itu? Jawabannya tidak soal rasa. Alasan terkuat konsumen memilihnya adalah ketersediaan — 95 persen. Lalu harga terjangkau (82 persen), kepraktisan (77 persen), dan rasa baru di urutan keempat (51 persen). Urutan ini menarik: ditemukan, murah, cepat — baru kemudian enak.

Bagi operator kopi keliling, maupun roastery dan supplier yang memasok mereka, implikasinya langsung. Bahan baku harus konsisten dari batch ke batch, resep cepat dieksekusi, dan margin bertahan pada harga jual terjangkau. Blend profil cokelat-kacang-karamel yang stabil saat dipadukan susu bukan lagi soal gaya — ia kebutuhan segmen. Paket B2B berisi roasted bean, resep standar, dan pelatihan menjadi produk tersendiri. Dan harga bertingkat antar segmen (kafe, kopi keliling, ritel) perlu dipikirkan sejak awal, karena sensitivitas harganya berbeda.

Sebagai catatan metodologis — penting dibaca sebelum mengutip: data Kemenperin adalah statistik industri nasional, sedangkan Jakpat dan Cimigo adalah survei konsumen dengan sampel terbatas (1.002 dan 247 responden). Angka survei tepat untuk membaca arah perilaku, bukan untuk mengestimasi populasi. Untuk keputusan investasi, survei ini perlu dilengkapi data primer.

Kesimpulan

Pasar kopi Indonesia tumbuh bukan karena orang Indonesia berganti selera, melainkan karena ngopi makin rutin — dan tiap kesempatan minum punya kanalnya sendiri. Konsumen rumah tetap setia pada instan. Konsumen kedai tetap datang untuk kumpul. Dan konsumen di perjalanan kini punya opsi racikan barista yang dulu tidak ada. Yang berubah bukan siapa yang menang, melainkan berapa banyak kesempatan ngopi yang kini bisa dilayani.

* * *

Sumber dan referensi:

• Kementerian Perindustrian RI — konsumsi 288 ribu ton (1,03 kg per kapita, 2025), proyeksi 3,61% (2024–2029), produksi kopi olahan 1,04 juta ton, ekspor 196,8 ribu ton (USD 661,9 juta) — https://www.kemenperin.go.id/ • Survei Jakpat 2025 (1.002 responden) — frekuensi, waktu, dan preferensi konsumsi kopi — https://jakpat.net/ • Survei Cimigo Oktober 2025 (247 responden) — kanal kopi racikan barista dan perilaku kopi keliling modern — https://www.cimigo.com/ • Data BPS via Kemenperin — struktur demografi Gen Z & milenial (2020) — https://www.bps.go.id/

Coffee Has Become a Habit, Shops Have Tripled — and the Fastest-Growing Channel Right Now Is on the Sidewalk

National coffee consumption of 288 thousand tonnes and 46% drink it daily. Shops have tripled, but the fastest-growing channel today is the sidewalk cart — through one simple thing.
By: Kabar Kopi Editorial | Ganjar Satyanagara · October 2026

The question rarely asked in Indonesia's coffee industry is not “is the market growing” — everyone knows it is. The right question is: in which segment is the growth happening, how fast, and what does it mean for each player?

Let me start with the most quoted and least digested figure. The Ministry of Industry recorded national coffee consumption in 2025 at 288 thousand tonnes, equivalent to 1.03 kg per capita, with a projected market growth of 3.61 percent per year through 2029. It sounds administrative. But behind it sits something worth noting: those 288 thousand tonnes are pure domestic absorption — and as our previous report showed, domestic demand is one of the factors keeping upstream prices high while global prices fall. The domestic market is no longer a complement to exports. It is the foundation.

Now to consumer behavior, because a market is not a number — a market is a habit.

Jakpat's 2025 survey of 1,002 respondents found that 46 percent of consumers drink coffee every day. Not every week. Every day. The favorite time is not the morning, as the Western stereotype goes, but the afternoon (35 percent) and after breakfast (34 percent). And the primary purpose is gathering and conversation (44 percent), not simply seeking caffeine for focus (34 percent).

This small detail matters. Coffee has become social infrastructure — a meeting place, a reason to gather, a filler of idle hours. But caution is needed here: the habit of an afternoon coffee with friends at a café, and the habit of brewing instant coffee at home before leaving for work, are two different habits — different places, different functions, and they do not replace each other. The Jakpat survey does record them in a single product-preference table: instant milk coffee consumed regularly by 53 percent of respondents, instant black coffee 43 percent, iced milk coffee from cafés 28 percent. These numbers are often read as if there were a “ladder” — from instant up to café. I read it differently. The three figures describe three different drinking occasions, not three levels of consumer maturity. There is a home market, there is a café market, and both are large in their own way.

And the café market itself is changing shape.

The Ministry of Industry recorded that the number of coffee shops has grown almost threefold in the last three years — supported by an extreme demographic structure, with more than 53 percent of Indonesia's population being Gen Z and millennials. But within the barista-brewed channel itself, a sub-channel is currently the fastest growing: the modern mobile coffee cart.

Cimigo's October 2025 survey — 247 respondents, a small but sharp sample — found that 49 percent of consumers drink barista-brewed coffee, with purchases averaging 4.5 times per week. Within the barista-brewed channel specifically: coffee shops remain the leading channel (88 percent), minimarkets 48 percent, and modern mobile coffee 47 percent.

One caution before reading that figure further: mobile coffee is not a replacement for the coffee shop. The person who spends two hours at a café over a meeting does not move to the sidewalk; conversely, a consumer who needs a quick barista-brewed coffee on the go often has no time to enter a café. Mobile coffee serves a drinking occasion that was previously unmet — it does not steal customers from cafés. The two grow in different occasions.

So why has mobile coffee grown so fast? The answer is not about taste. The strongest reason consumers choose it is availability — 95 percent. Followed by affordable price (82 percent), practicality (77 percent), and taste only in fourth place (51 percent). The order is telling: found, cheap, fast — and only then tasty.

For mobile coffee operators, and for roasteries and suppliers who supply them, the implications are immediate. Raw material must be consistent from batch to batch, recipes fast to execute, and margins sustainable at an affordable selling price. A chocolate-nut-caramel blend profile that stays stable with milk is no longer a style choice — it is a segment requirement. A B2B package of roasted beans, standard recipes, and training becomes a product in its own right. And tiered pricing across segments (café, mobile, retail) needs to be designed from the start, because price sensitivity differs.

A methodological note — important to read before quoting: Ministry of Industry data is national industrial statistics, while Jakpat and Cimigo are consumer surveys with limited samples (1,002 and 247 respondents). Survey figures are appropriate for reading behavioral direction, not for precise population estimates. For investment decisions, these surveys need to be complemented with primary data.

Conclusion

Indonesia's coffee market is growing not because Indonesians are changing their tastes, but because coffee drinking is becoming more routine — and every drinking occasion has its own channel. Home consumers remain loyal to instant. Café-goers still come to gather. And consumers on the move now have a barista-brewed option that did not exist before. What has changed is not who wins, but how many drinking occasions can now be served.

* * *

Sources and references:

• Ministry of Industry, Republic of Indonesia — consumption of 288 thousand tonnes (1.03 kg per capita, 2025), growth projection of 3.61% (2024–2029), processed coffee output of 1.04 million tonnes, exports of 196.8 thousand tonnes (USD 661.9 million) — https://www.kemenperin.go.id/ • Jakpat Survey 2025 (1,002 respondents) — coffee consumption frequency, timing, and preferences — https://jakpat.net/ • Cimigo Survey October 2025 (247 respondents) — barista-brewed coffee channels and mobile coffee behavior — https://www.cimigo.com/ • BPS data via Ministry of Industry — Gen Z & millennial demographic structure (2020) — https://www.bps.go.id/

articles.content_id:
Dari Roastery ke Cangkir: Strategi Bertahan dan Tumbuh Saat Harga Kopi Tembus Rekor

Harga green bean tertinggi dalam 50 tahun menekan margin roastery, penjual eceran, dan coffee shop. Artikel ini memotret siapa yang paling rentan — dan empat langkah praktis untuk tetap tumbuh di tengah tekanan.
Oleh: Redaksi Kabar Kopi | Ganjar Satyanagara · 7 Oktober 2026

Margin bisnis kopi dihilir sedang diserang dari dua arah. Harga green bean naik ke level tertinggi dalam 50 tahun, sementara konsumen tidak serta-merta bersedia membayar lebih.

Saya menyadari beratnya situasi ini ketika membaca laporan Kontan Insight (2026): margin emiten sebesar MYOR dan FORE berpotensi tertekan karena kenaikan harga bahan baku tidak sepenuhnya bisa diteruskan ke harga jual. Jika perusahaan sebesar itu saja kepayahan, apa kabar roastery kecil di pinggir kota, atau coffee shop tiga cabang yang harus bayar sewa tiap bulan?

KopiTime dan AgroIndonesia mencatat penyebabnya: defisit pasokan akibat cuaca buruk di Brasil, Vietnam, dan sebagian Indonesia; stok global yang tipis setelah beberapa musim panen lemah; pelemahan dolar AS yang mendorong pembeli non-USD; serta bayangan El Niño dan La Niña yang bergantian datang. Rekomendasi harga arabika dari Vibiznews (September–Oktober 2026) menempatkan kita pada posisi yang secara historis tinggi. Singkatnya: tekanan ini bukan badai sesaat, dan bersiap menghadapinya adalah satu-satunya pilihan.

Tidak semua pelaku hilir berada di perahu yang sama

Roaster specialty, menurut saya, berada di posisi paling nyaman. Konsumennya sudah terbiasa membayar lebih dan bisa menerima kenaikan harga — asal dijelaskan dengan baik. Narasi iklim, kelangkaan, kualitas: semuanya bisa dikomunikasikan. Bahkan ada peluang di sini. Micro-lot, proses eksperimental seperti anaerobik dan wine process, traceability yang transparan — fase harga tinggi justru menjadi alasan untuk naik kelas.

Roaster komersial tidak semujur itu. Segmennya sensitif harga; menaikkan harga sedikit saja bisa membuat pelanggan pindah ke kompetitor. Jalan tengahnya adalah optimasi blend arabika-robusta berkualitas dan efisiensi operasional, sambil tetap menjaga konsistensi rasa yang menjadi alasan pelanggan bertahan.

Penjual eceran berada di tengah-tengah. Brand yang kuat dan punya loyalitas pelanggan masih punya ruang; brand tanpa diferensiasi akan terasa tekanannya paling dulu. Bundling, subscription, dan edukasi konsumen adalah tiga hal yang bisa langsung dijalankan tanpa menunggu harga kembali turun.

Coffee shop punya ruang gerak yang berbeda lagi. COGS memang terasa pada menu espresso dan manual brew, tapi mereka menjual lebih dari kopi — experience, tempat, cerita. Diversifikasi menu ke non-kopi dan signature drink, optimasi porsi, serta narasi keberlanjutan bisa menaikkan rata-rata transaksi tanpa perlu menaikkan harga kopi itu sendiri.

Empat langkah yang bisa dijalankan sekarang

Pertama, pisahkan strategi harga. Produk specialty bisa naik lebih berani dengan narasi origin yang kuat. Produk komersial peruh perlakuan lebih hati-hati: uji kenaikan bertahap pada produk andalan, lalu pantau respons pelanggan sebelum menyentuh yang lain.

Kedua, komunikasikan harga lewat nilai. Konsumen tidak keberatan membayar lebih; mereka keberatan dibuat tidak paham. Jelaskan alasan kenaikan — iklim, pasokan global, kualitas — dan tampilkan informasi origin, proses, serta cup score pada kemasan dan menu. Transparansi adalah strategi pricing yang paling murah.

Ketiga, kelola stok dan supplier dengan serius. Jangan bergantung pada satu sumber. Bangun hubungan jangka panjang dengan beberapa supplier kunci, pertimbangkan kontrak forward untuk volume inti, dan diversifikasikan origin untuk mengurangi risiko gagal panen lokal.

Keempat, diferensiasikan. Untuk roaster specialty: micro-lot, cupping event, subscription model. Untuk roaster komersial: konsistensi rasa dan convenience seperti pod, capsule, dan ready-to-drink. Untuk coffee shop: experience yang membuat pelanggan kembali bukan karena harga — latte art, brewing class, cerita di balik setiap cangkir.

Penutup

Saya tidak akan berpura-pura fase ini mudah. Margin yang menyempit adalah kenyataan, dan tidak ada satu pun strategi yang mengembalikan harga ke titik semula. Tapi setiap kali membaca laporan-laporan ini, saya kembali pada satu kesimpulan yang sama.

Tekanan harga memaksa bisnis untuk jujur pada dirinya sendiri: apa yang sebenarnya kita jual? Jika jawabannya sekadar kopi, harga akan selalu jadi pertarungan. Jika jawabannya cerita, kualitas, dan pengalaman — harga tinggi bukan akhir, melainkan undangan untuk naik kelas.

* * *

Report oleh:

• Redaksi Kabar Kopi — Report by MEVO, 7 Oktober 2026

articles.content_en:
From Roastery to Cup: Strategies to Survive and Grow When Coffee Prices Hit Records

Green bean prices at a 50-year high are squeezing margins for roasteries, retailers, and coffee shops. This article maps who is most vulnerable — and four practical steps to keep growing under pressure.
By: Kabar Kopi Editorial | Ganjar Satyanagara · October 7, 2026

Margins in the coffee downstream are being squeezed from two directions at once. Green bean prices have climbed to their highest level in 50 years, while consumers are not automatically willing to pay more.

I began to grasp how heavy this pressure is when I read Kontan Insight's 2026 report: margins at companies as large as MYOR and FORE could come under pressure, because rising raw material costs cannot be fully passed on to retail prices. If even corporations of that size are struggling, what about a small roastery on the edge of town, or a three-branch coffee shop that has to pay rent every month?

KopiTime and AgroIndonesia have traced the causes: supply deficits from poor weather in Brazil, Vietnam, and parts of Indonesia; thin global stocks after several weak harvests; a weakening US dollar that lifts demand from non-USD buyers; and the shadow of alternating El Niño and La Niña. Arabika price recommendations from Vibiznews (September–October 2026) place us at historically high levels. In short, this is not a passing storm, and preparing for it is the only option.

Not all downstream players are in the same boat

Specialty roasters, in my view, sit in the most comfortable position. Their consumers are used to paying more and can accept price increases — as long as they are explained well. Climate narratives, scarcity, quality: all of these can be communicated. There is even opportunity here. Micro-lots, experimental processes like anaerobic and wine process, transparent traceability — a high-price phase is precisely the reason to move up a class.

Commercial roasters are not so fortunate. Their segment is price-sensitive; raising prices even slightly can send customers to competitors. The middle path is optimizing quality arabica-robusta blends and operational efficiency, while keeping the consistent taste that gives customers a reason to stay.

Retail sellers sit somewhere in between. Brands with strength and customer loyalty still have room; brands without differentiation will feel the pressure first. Bundling, subscriptions, and consumer education are three things that can be started right now, without waiting for prices to fall back.

Coffee shops move differently again. COGS certainly bites into espresso and manual brew menus, but they sell more than coffee — experience, space, stories. Menu diversification into non-coffee and signature drinks, portion optimization, and sustainability narratives can raise average tickets without touching the price of the coffee itself.

Four steps that can be taken now

First, separate your pricing strategies. Specialty products can be raised more boldly with strong origin narratives. Commercial products need a gentler touch: test gradual increases on flagship products, then watch customer response before touching anything else.

Second, communicate price through value. Consumers don't mind paying more; they mind being left in the dark. Explain the reasons for increases — climate, global supply, quality — and show origin, process, and cup score information on packaging and menus. Transparency is the cheapest pricing strategy there is.

Third, manage stock and suppliers seriously. Don't depend on a single source. Build long-term relationships with several key suppliers, consider forward contracts for core volume, and diversify origins to reduce the risk of local crop failure.

Fourth, differentiate. For specialty roasters: micro-lots, cupping events, subscription models. For commercial roasters: consistent taste and convenience like pods, capsules, and ready-to-drink. For coffee shops: an experience that brings customers back for more than the price — latte art, brewing classes, the story behind every cup.

Closing

I won't pretend this phase is easy. Shrinking margins are a reality, and no single strategy will return prices to where they were. But every time I read these reports, I keep arriving at the same conclusion.

Price pressure forces a business to be honest with itself: what are we actually selling? If the answer is merely coffee, price will always be a battle. If the answer is story, quality, and experience — high prices are not an end, but an invitation to move up a class.

* * *

Report by:

• Kabar Kopi Editorial — Report by MEVO, October 7, 2026
